# Averitt adds 100,000-sq.ft. Warehouse to Mississippi Freight Campus

Written by WarehouseArc Newsroom • August 28, 2026

Averitt has opened a 100,000-square-foot warehouse beside its existing 57-door LTL terminal in Richland, Mississippi, putting distribution, fulfillment and asset-based freight operations on the same logistics campus.

The Jackson Distribution & Fulfillment facility opened August 24 at 109 Diane Drive, near the intersection of Interstates 20 and 55.

Rather than operating solely as a dedicated warehouse for a single customer, the building is configured as a multi-tenant facility where Averitt is offering space without long-term warehouse contracts.

That gives the 3PL capacity for customers seeking temporary inventory space as well as more conventional distribution and fulfillment operations. Averitt is marketing the building for requirements including overflow inventory, seasonal storage and emergency staging, with customers able to adjust the amount of space they use as requirements change.

The operational proposition extends beyond the additional square footage.

# Inside Our New 210,000 Sq. Ft. Deltaport Warehouse

 by Bill Heaney | Logistics 

Every hour a container sits is an hour of cost. Demurrage clocks, per diem charges, congested truck gates, and long drayage runs to inland warehouses all quietly erode margin on freight that has already crossed an ocean. For importers moving volume through the Pacific Gateway, the distance between the terminal gate and the first set of dock doors matters more than almost any other variable in the inbound supply chain.

That is exactly the gap our newest facility closes. As of August 1, 2026, 18 Wheels Warehousing and Trucking has taken possession of a 210,000 square foot distribution facility at 3995 27B Avenue in Delta (Tsawwassen), positioned directly adjacent to Deltaport, Canada's primary container terminal. It is one of the shortest drayage moves available to shippers arriving through Metro Vancouver, and it is now part of our national network.

Translink Express Logistics has made four senior leadership appointments and announced plans to transform its Narborough headquarters into a major indoor palletised freight sortation centre.

 R By Ryan Fowler Publisher 

 1st September 2026 3 min read 

Translink Express Logistics has appointed four senior leaders as the Leicestershire logistics firm prepares for further growth ahead of its 40th anniversary.

The business has promoted Lee Barrett to head of traffic, Dan Green to the newly created role of head of project management and Shanice Walsh to head of operations.

Ryan Wallis has also joined the company as head of warehousing.

The appointments follow growth of almost 32% over the past 2 years, driven by new customer wins and existing customers increasing their use of Translink Express Logistics services.
